body_md:

label: lem-sliding-strong
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the Sobolev embedding, $v$ is differentiable a.e. Suppose that $x_1\in E\cap A_0(v)$ and that $v$ is differentiable at $x_1$. Let $P$ be the corresponding paraboloid touching $\Gamma_v^0$ from below at $x_0\in F$, so that $P+t$ touches
$v$ from below at $x_1$ for some $t>0$.
Let $L$ be a supporting affine function to $\Gamma_v^0$ at $x_1$. Since both $L$ and $P+t$ touch $v$ from below at $x_1$, we have $DL=Dv(x_1)=DP(x_1)$. The concavity of $P$ gives $P+t\leq L$, and hence
\begin{equation*}
    \Gamma_v^0(x_0)=P(x_0)<P(x_0)+t \leq L(x_0)\leq\Gamma_v^0(x_0),
\end{equation*}
a contradiction. Thus, $v$ is not differentiable at any point of $E\cap A_0(v)$, and the conclusion follows.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first assume that $u\in W^{2,n}(B_1)$, so that $u\in C(\overline{B}_1)$ by the Sobolev embedding. Under the normalization \eqref{eq-global-normalization},
we define the contact sets as in Step 1 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm-log-hessian-estimate}. The same argument gives \eqref{eq-global-interior-contact}.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem-nonhomo-measure-est-strong} instead of Lemma~\ref{lem-nonhomo-measure-est}, we obtain \eqref{eq-global-measure}. The same summation and normalization arguments then prove the estimate.

For a general
$u\in W^{2,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_1)\cap L^\infty(B_1)$ and $r\in(1/2,1)$, let $ u_r(x)=u(rx)$, $\lambda_r(x)=\lambda(rx)$ and $f_r(x)=r^2f(rx)$. Then $u_r\in W^{2,n}(B_1)$ is an $L^n$-strong supersolution with ellipticity $\lambda_r$ and right-hand side $f_r$. Applying the preceding estimate to $u_r$ and letting $r\to1^-$, we conclude by the monotone convergence theorem, as in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm-log-hessian-estimate}.

label: rmk-Grushin-exponent
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk-Grushin-exponent}
The following example illustrates the essential dependence
of regularity on the sign of $\gamma$, and shows that the
H\"older exponents in Proposition~\ref{prop-Grushin-strong}
are sharp for $\gamma<0$ and nearly sharp for $\gamma>0$.


For $0<|\gamma|<n_1/(n(n-1))$, consider
\begin{equation*}
    w_{\gamma}(y,z)
    \coloneqq
    \frac{z_1^2}{2}
    -\frac{|y|^{2-\gamma}}{(2-\gamma)(n_1-\gamma)}.
\end{equation*}
Then we have $\Delta_yw_{\gamma}=-|y|^{-\gamma}$ and $\Delta_zw_{\gamma}=1$ for $y \neq 0$, and hence $G_{\gamma}w_{\gamma}=0$ a.e. Since $w_{\gamma}\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,n}(B_1)$, it follows that $w_{\gamma}$ is an $L^n$-strong solution of the Grushin equation covered by Proposition~\ref{prop-Grushin-strong}.

The function $w_{\gamma}$ is smooth in $z$.
When $\gamma<0$, it belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,-\gamma}$
and has no higher H\"older exponent for its second derivatives
across $\{y=0\}$.
When $\gamma>0$, it belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,1-\gamma}$
but not to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,\beta}$ for any
$\beta \in (1-\gamma, 1)$.
